Projects

Meta Vision

2026

An iOS assistive-reading prototype designed to help blind and low-vision users capture documents, verify recognized text, and listen to it quickly and accurately.

  • On-device reading pipeline: Captures a document with the iPhone camera, checks image quality, performs OCR, and speaks the result.
  • AI-assisted verification: Uses an imported on-device Gemma model through LiteRT-LM to verify and summarize recognized text.
  • Accessible controls: Supports repeat, stop, adjustable speech speed, and an on-device reading history.
  • Wearable roadmap: Integration with Meta Ray-Ban glasses and hands-free voice commands is planned.

Monocle

2026

A native macOS menu-bar app that helps blind and low-vision users magnify on-screen content, recognize text, and hear it read aloud.

  • Live magnification: A circular magnifier follows the pointer using ScreenCaptureKit.
  • On-device accessibility: Apple Vision handles OCR and AVFoundation provides spoken reading, keeping everyday use private and local.
  • Keyboard-first controls: Global shortcuts make OCR capture and reading available without interrupting the current workflow.
  • Optional AI descriptions: Users can explicitly request a screen description using their own OpenAI API key, stored securely in Keychain.

B-Counting

2026

An accessible, command-driven desktop accounting application designed primarily for blind and low-vision users.

  • Guided command workflow: Combines the speed of commands such as new, summary, and find with one-question-at-a-time forms and review-before-save safeguards.
  • Screen-reader first: Uses semantic controls, predictable focus, concise announcements, and complete keyboard navigation.
  • Portable records: Stores transactions in documented, human-readable JSON Lines, with CSV export and a clear audit trail.
  • Focused first release: Prioritizes reliable transaction entry, search, summaries, categorization, export, and backup over complex bookkeeping features.

Blog

My NUS Young Fellowship Experience

2026

I recently completed the NUS Young Fellowship Programme at the National University of Singapore, representing the Department of Statistics, University of Colombo.

The fellowship brought together 112 young participants from more than 26 countries across five continents. One of the most rewarding parts of the experience was meeting, learning from, and building friendships with inspiring people from different cultures, disciplines, and walks of life.

Throughout the programme, I experienced many sides of NUS—from research and innovation to entrepreneurship, industry engagement, and its vibrant international community.

Highlights

  • Research and technical sessions led by NUS faculty.
  • An industry visit to Seagate Singapore, where we learned about data-storage technology, chip design, and advances in lithography.
  • An introduction to GRIP, the Graduate Research Innovation Programme.
  • Inspiring conversations with NUS alumni founders about turning research into deep-tech ventures.
  • Cross-cultural group projects that challenged us to exchange ideas and approach problems from new perspectives.

More than anything, the fellowship was about stepping into a new environment, listening to different perspectives, and creating meaningful connections with people from around the world. I am truly grateful for the learning, friendships, memories, and experiences I gained during my time at NUS. It is an experience I will carry with me for a long time. 🇸🇬
